gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch directly addresses the stated issue by restructuring MemoryBuildOptions from flat fields (conversationChunking, insightBuild, boundaryDetector) into nested ExtractionOptions and RetrievalOptions groups. It creates ~13 new record classes for the grouped options, modifies DefaultMemory to accept and use MemoryBuildOptions for deriving default ExtractionConfig and RetrievalConfig, updates the builder to pass options through, simplifies DeepStrategyConfig.QueryExpansionConfig from 3 fields to 1, and updates examples to use the new nested API. This aligns well with the issue requirements for grouped extraction/retrieval defaults propagated through DefaultMemory.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The base will fail: the test patch introduces imports and calls to types that don't exist in the base (e.g., ExtractionOptions, RetrievalOptions, SimpleRetrievalOptions, DeepRetrievalOptions, etc.), references a 9-parameter DefaultMemory constructor that doesn't exist, and uses QueryExpansionConfig(int) with 1 parameter instead of the base's 3-parameter constructor. Compilation will fail before any tests run. The gold patch provides all necessary types and constructors so tests should compile and pass.
too_narrow_risks: Extraction insightEnabled propagation is not directly tested via DefaultMemory (only checked at the MemoryBuildOptions defaults level)
Simple retrieval rawDataTopK and insightTopK propagation through DefaultMemory.retrieve() with SIMPLE strategy is not tested
Deep retrieval rerank config propagation (toRerankConfig method) is not tested end-to-end
No test verifies that the old 6-parameter and 8-parameter DefaultMemory constructors still work (backwards compatibility)
implementation_coupling: builderPropagatesOptionsIntoDefaultMemory uses readField(memory, 'buildOptions', MemoryBuildOptions.class) which couples to the exact private field name 'buildOptions' in the gold patch — an alternative using 'options' or 'config' would fail
Tests construct DefaultMemory directly via a 9-parameter constructor specific to the gold implementation — alternative implementations using a factory or different constructor shape would not compile
QueryExpansionConfig simplification from 3 fields to 1 is prescriptive — tests enforce this exact record shape rather than observable behavior
environment_risks: Maven build required (mvn test-compile and mvn test) — Docker image should have all dependencies cached, but network-dependent resolution could fail if not
Test compilation depends on all new record classes being present — a partial implementation missing any one class will cause full test-compile failure for all tests

evidence.detail: Issue requires grouped extraction/retrieval options in MemoryBuildOptions, with DefaultMemory using them for defaults
Gold patch creates ~13 new option records, modifies MemoryBuildOptions, DefaultMemory, DefaultMemoryBuilder, MemoryExtractionAssembler, DeepStrategyConfig, and two examples

Test patch modifies 7 test files: adds new tests for builder-level defaults propagation (extraction: scope/timeout/language/foresight, retrieval: timeout/cache/topK), nested option structure, builder propagation via reflection, and simplified QueryExpansionConfig
Base has flat conversationChunking/insightBuild/boundaryDetector fields — tests reference nested extraction()/retrieval() methods that don't exist, ensuring base fails compilation
Base QueryExpansionConfig has 3 fields (maxExpandedQueries, originalWeight, expandedWeight); test patch uses single-arg constructor, ensuring base fails compilation
Runs 7 specific test classes via Maven — scoped to affected code, no full-suite regression

summary: Solid instance with well-scoped tests that cover the core requirements: nested option structure defaults, extraction config propagation (scope, timeout, language, foresight), retrieval config propagation (simple: timeout/cache/tier2.topK, deep: timeout/cache/tier2.topK/sufficiency), builder-to-DefaultMemory propagation, and assembler rewiring. Base correctly fails (missing types/constructors). Minor implementation coupling exists through reflection-based field name checks and the specific 9-parameter constructor, which could reject alternative implementations that achieve the same observable behavior with different internal structure. However, given the structural nature of the refactoring task, this level of coupling is largely acceptable. Test coverage has small gaps (rerank propagation, some topK propagation paths) but covers the most important aspects of the change.
